newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ICI Australia to buy back shares from parent.
newsitem.headline: ICI Australia to buy back shares from parent.

text.p: ICI Australia Ltd said on Friday it proposes to buy back up to A$360 million (US$275 million) worth of its own shares from its U.K. parent, Imperial Chemical Industries Plc, at a price of up to A$11.96 per share.

The U.K. company said earlier this month it planned to sell its 62.4 percent stake in ICI Australia, a producer of chemicals, explosives, plastics, paints and fertilisers, to help it buy Uniliver's specialty chemicals business for US$8 billion.

"The directors believe that the benefits to non-associated shareholders of the buyback include an increase in earnings and cash flow per share, the favourable buyback pricing mechanism, and the resultant increase in the underlying value of remaining ICI Australia shares," ICI Australia said.
ICI Australia shares rose 19 cents to A$12.30 on the news.
ICI Australia said it planned to form an agreement with ICI Plc, covering intellectual property, technology, supply and distribution arrangements.
"The directors believe that, with the exception of some one-off separation costs, these arrangements, will be neutral to positive for ICI Australia," ICI Australia said.
The company said it would make a further announcement on these arrangements as soon as relevant agreements were executed.
ICI Australia said an extraordinary general meeting will be held on June 25 to vote on the buyback proposal.

ICI Australia, with a market capitalisation of about A$3.6 billion, reported a net profit of A$110.7 million in the half year to March 31, up from A$92.6 million a year earlier. Profit for the year to September 30, 1996 was A$197.1 million.
